title: Floppy I/O and the FAT read side (kernel/disk.inc, kernel/dskwin.inc, kernel/drvvol.inc; SPEC.md 18, 19)
summary: The read side is in good shape as a mechanism. dsk_xfer is one transfer routine for both directions and every volume kind. A hostile-BPB table turns every divide that runs under sch_lock into a refusal. One track-to-end sector cache sits under disk_read and is invalidated at the one write choke point. A FAT window is keyed by a signature that os88disk.py now makes unique per shipped image. Batching is measured on the 5150, and so is the fix that stopped trusting AL. Three weaknesses sit at the edges rather than in the core loop. (1) The boot partition is mounted with int 13h AH=08h geometry while boothd and dsk_bpb_check address it with the BPB's, which is FIELD-NOTES 33's disagreement still live in the kernel. (2) Two safety arguments are written down but not enforced: the batch bracket assumes the caller holds the gfx lock, yet a published slot opens it unchecked; and a run past the buffer's 64KB segment wraps silently. (3) The retry ladder treats a speculative read-ahead fill like a real read, so one bad sector at a track's end taxes every access to that track. It also discards status 06h, the one swap signal an AT gives for free. A caller-held FIND cursor is cheap now, because dsk_dscan already resumes from a raw slot. The biggest defect is documentation drift. The file header, the disk_read, disk_mount, dsk_sortdir, dsk_chdir_q and fdd_probe headers, about ten orphaned headers for deleted routines, dskwin.inc's banner, and SPEC 18's intro, symbol tables and 18.3 mount sequence still describe replaced designs: one sector per call, the FAT snapshot, disk_dir and disk_icons, the fixed-address listing, dsk_relist, unit 1 only, the 128KB gate, and byte-identical boot sectors. Verified: 61 doc fixes confirmed (two of the reviewer's refuted as code changes, seven added); of 20 findings 12 confirmed, 4 corrected (dr-8's fix would itself overflow a div, dr-14 must keep clearing the probed unit's bit), none refuted, 4 unchecked.

strengths.title: One transfer routine, one retry policy
strengths.why: Read and write differ by one byte, so CHS, cylinder guard, DMA bounce, EOT write and retries exist once; the cache fill and the mounted-image arm re-enter it and carry no CHS code of their own

strengths.title: Divide safety is arithmetic
strengths.why: cmp dx,cx / jae before the CHS div and cmp dx,bx / jae before the cluster-count div turn a #DE under sch_lock into a refusal; every derived-layout add is carry-checked

strengths.title: BPB table names the consumer each rule protects
strengths.why: Hostile-input validation in a documented order; several rules are range tests that are short and also correct at 0

strengths.title: dsk_runcap's 17-bit negation
strengths.why: DMA-page and BX-wrap caps with no zero test; a 0 result becomes a one-sector bounce through a 512-aligned dsk_secbuf that an %error enforces

strengths.title: CF=0 is the contract, not AL
strengths.why: A 5150-measured fix (AL=1 for a 9-sector read) that removed a revolution per sector; the A/B knob is kept

strengths.title: The cache mirrors the disk
strengths.why: Invalidation hangs off disk_write so no future write can forget it. It fills from the requested sector to the track's end by measurement, keeps a pollution gate, skips a page-straddling slot, uses a one-sector second chance in place of LRU, and was simulated before it was built

strengths.title: Size-driven chain walk, no EOC constants
strengths.why: Each pass consumes at least one sector, so a cyclic FAT cannot hang it; runs are kept in clusters, so 32-bit volumes cost the walk nothing; the directory walker has its own sector bound

strengths.title: Owned DPT with per-call EOT
strengths.why: DOS's fix done properly: the table is copied rather than replaced, so this machine's timings stand, and EOT follows the mounted volume's spt

strengths.title: The presence probe fails toward keeping a drive
strengths.why: It retires a drive only on the positive ST0=7x absence shape seen in the field; the asymmetric-cost argument is the model for any destructive probe

strengths.title: Instruments ship with the design
strengths.why: The DD block, the (LBA, run) trace, the per-phase counters, the field-labelled failure toast and the fdd ST rows are what made the AL bug, the head-crossing write and ST0 findable off real iron

strengths.title: Layout couplings are %errors
strengths.why: Every place that reads two cells as one is asserted, so a reorder breaks the build rather than the machine

findings.title: Boot partition mounted with AH=08h geometry while the volume is addressed with the BPB's
findings.detail: dsk_boot_from_x (.ovl) stores int 13h AH=08h's spt/heads in dsk_bootspt/dsk_boothds. disk_mount_x loads them into disk_spt/disk_heads for a BIOS hard-disk row and so for the one read that fetches the BPB (LBA 0 plus [dsk_vbase]). dsk_bpb_check then switches disk_spt/heads to the BPB's. boothd was changed to BPB geometry because AH=08h was the wrong invariant (FIELD-NOTES 33). When the volume was written with a geometry the drive's ROM does not answer (FN33's 17/4 volume on a 63/16 drive), LBA = base maps to a different CHS under the ROM geometry, the kernel's first read lands elsewhere, the BPB fails, and C: never mounts. dsk_bootspt=0 drops to 9/2, which is worse. Hibernate (hiber.inc) and DSK_HCYLPROBE's dsk_hcyl_probe also read the pair.
evidence: kernel/disk.inc:4074-4081 used for the BPB fetch
boot/boothd.asm:16-31 BPB geometry is the invariant
boot/boothd.asm:286-288 hand-off passes DL, BX:CX only
findings.recommendation: Have boothd hand over its BPB spt/heads (it holds [spt] and [bpb_heads]) in SI/DI, with a marker in AX so an older BOOTHD.SYS is detected. dsk_boot_from_x uses them when the marker matches and falls back to AH=08h otherwise; delete the fallback once every boothd carries the marker. Verify on the FN33 dumped images in 86Box first, because this is predicted from reading, not from a run.
findings.bytes_est: +8 boothd; +6 .ovl now, -28 .ovl once AH=08h goes; 0 resident
findings.prior_art: DOS IO.SYS builds the fixed-disk BDS from one source and uses it for every access; os8088's boot sector and kernel disagree
findings.verify_note: Re-read 2744-2807, 4074-4081, 5326-5330 and boothd.asm 16-31/286-288: the kernel's BPB fetch uses AH=08h's answer while boothd and dsk_bpb_check use the BPB's. It bites only when the two geometries differ and the base is not 0, which is FN33's shape exactly; FN33 says both images BOOT with the new sector, which does not establish that C: mounts. Not in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE.

findings.title: Batch bracket's 'UI is frozen' assertion is not enforced at a door packages can call
findings.detail: dsk_batch_begin_x sets the batch unconditionally. Inside one, a floppy's banked BPB and signature, the banked FAT window and the cache are trusted with no LBA 0 read. The whole safety argument is 'any gfx_unlock ends it', which assumes the caller holds the gfx lock. The door is a published slot (0x02B0, dkf_dsk_batch_begin) with a C thunk, and package file I/O is documented as not holding the mutex. So a package-opened batch survives until the next unlock anywhere, which on an idle desktop can be a long time, and a swapped floppy is then written with the old disk's FAT. No package in this tree calls it; the in-tree callers (compress.inc, drivers/hdd/inst.inc) run under the lock.
evidence: kernel/fprog.inc:633-646 package file I/O holds no mutex
findings.recommendation: dsk_batch_begin_x does nothing unless [gfx_lock_flag] is set and [gfx_lock_own] == [sch_cur], using fpg_arm's test (fprog.inc:616-620). A refused begin is only slower. Check drivers/hdd/inst.inc's two begins still pass (they rely on the callback's lock).
findings.verify_note: dsk_batch_begin_x (940-953) has no lock test and the slot is published with a C thunk; gfx_unlock's store at vga12.inc:5191 is the only end. Byte estimate raised from +12: cmp/je/mov/cmp/jne is 16 bytes.

findings.title: A failing read-ahead fill runs the full retry ladder, then the direct read runs it again
findings.detail: A miss fills to the track's end through disk_read_x and gets 3 attempts at the run, then the single-sector fallback - and after each single sector succeeds, the next pass recomputes a full run and fails three times again, so a bad sector at the track's tail costs a ladder per good sector before it. A bad sector in the speculative tail fails the fill, the slot stays empty, and the direct read retries the wanted sectors. Because nothing was cached, every later read on that track refills and pays the failing tail again: one marginal sector nobody asked for taxes all its good neighbours with resets.
evidence: kernel/disk.inc:7023-7029 CF=1 falls to direct read
kernel/disk.inc:4202-4204 rah_busy also marks the LBA 0 swap-detector read, which needs its ladder
findings.recommendation: Mark a fill distinctly (for example add/sub 2 on dsk_rah_busy instead of inc/dec; every reader tests it against 0, and 1708 reads it as a word with dsk_lbahi) and have dsk_xfer's failure arm fail a fill at its first error, with no reset and no ladder. Optionally cache the good prefix already read.
findings.verify_note: dsk_rah_fill calls disk_read_x with only inc dsk_rah_busy (7206); dsk_xfer's failure arm (2020-2073) has no fill test. The cost is somewhat worse than stated, since a successful single-sector retry returns to full-length runs.

findings.title: Status 06h (media changed) is retried as a generic error and discarded
findings.detail: On AT-class BIOSes the first access after a change-line rise answers AH=06h. dsk_xfer resets and retries, the retry succeeds, and the only hardware swap signal is lost: a write after a fast swap (inside a quiet switch whose motor test passed, or a batch) goes to the new disk with the old FAT. The change line was declined before as a REPLACEMENT for the motor test (AH=16h; XTs have none). This is additive and free, because it arrives on a read already being made.
findings.recommendation: On AH=06h with [dsk_mntok]=1 (inside a validated mount), clear [dsk_mntok] so the next operation remounts and the write gate shuts, and fail the transfer with ioerr 06h and no retry. During a mount ([dsk_mntok]=0) keep today's retry, since the mount re-validates anyway.
findings.prior_art: DOS 3.2+ 'Invalid disk change' via int 24h; AmigaOS disk-change interrupt to the filesystem
findings.verify_note: dsk_xfer special-cases 03h alone (2025-2027); 06h takes the reset-and-retry path. Whether a given AT ROM reports 06h with CF=1 to the caller is still the open question the area doc lists.

findings.title: OSAPI_FILE_FIND stays quadratic though dsk_dscan already resumes from a raw slot
findings.detail: dsk_find_x calls dsk_dscan with CX=0 and an ordinal, so N entries cost N(N+1)/2 visits. dsk_dscan already takes a raw slot to start at and answers the next one, and fcp_scan uses it that way. A FILE_FIND_SEQ with READ_SEQ's caller-held 16-byte cursor (folder cluster, raw slot, [dsk_mgen]) is a thin wrapper. Being caller-held, it survives the find/read/write/find loop that dsk_find's header rejected a kernel cursor for. SPEC.md 18.95.2 retired the cursor on I/O grounds only and says what remains is CPU; DISK-CPU-PLAN 3.1 measured that CPU.
findings.recommendation: Add a FILE_FIND_SEQ cell at the end of the table (kern_big, DSK_DSCAN): check the generation, call dsk_dscan(slot,0), write the next slot back into the cursor.
findings.listed_as: DISK-CPU-PLAN.md 3.1 (new: the body already exists, so the cost is a wrapper)
findings.prior_art: DOS FindFirst/FindNext keeps the search state in the caller's DTA
findings.verify_note: dsk_find_x passes CX=0 and BP=ordinal to dsk_dscan (8034-8038); dsk_dscan takes a raw slot in CX. The design choice in SPEC 19.7.1/18.95.2 is about revolutions, not CPU, so it does not answer this.

findings.title: Fixed overhead on every dsk_xfer, cache hits included
findings.detail: Every call pays dsk_media_ok (row lookup and BDA reads), a far call to fpg_busy, a second dsk_vol_row_x, and the vbase and cylmax loads: about 600-700 cycles (about 0.14 ms on the 5150), against a cache hit's 1.6 ms copy. Fill and .img re-entries pay it again. dsk_media_ok is asked only to choose FPG_WARM.
findings.recommendation: Skip dsk_media_ok when the widget is already armed (FPG_ARMED), and have it hand back the row so the second lookup goes.
findings.listed_as: DISK-CPU-PLAN.md 7 (the read path's cycles a KB)
findings.verify_note: The call sequence at 1405-1460 is as described; the cycle and byte figures were not re-derived.

findings.title: A run past the buffer's segment wraps to ES:0000 silently
findings.detail: dsk_runcap caps at the BX wrap, but .notched then adds the run to BX (wrapping to 0) with ES unchanged, and the next dsk_runcap at BX=0 answers a full 128-sector cap. 'A transfer is at most 128 sectors' and 'the caller's budget must cover count*512' are prose. Today's callers stay bounded only because they convert a 16-bit byte count.
findings.recommendation: At .notched, fail when add bx,ax carries while SI != 0. This runs once per int 13h call, not per sector.
findings.verify_note: dsk_runcap's BX arm gives 128 at BX=0 (neg 0 / cmc / rcr / shr 8); .notched's add bx,ax has no carry test.

findings.title: dsk_rah_fill computes the track phase on the volume-relative LBA, not LBA+base
findings.detail: The fill divides DI by spt while the transfer converts DI+[dsk_base]. On a BIOS boot partition not aligned to a track (a foreign FDISK's 1MB alignment), the fill is mis-sized and splits into two int 13h calls or under-fills. The data stays correct. The installer's head-1-sector-1 layout is aligned. Only BIOS rows are affected: dsk_xfer never consults the cache for a DVK_DRV volume (1714-1716).
findings.recommendation: Fold the base in without a straight 32/16 div by spt: (base+DI)/spt can exceed a word on a partition past ~65,536 x spt sectors (4M on 63 spt) and would #DE under sch_lock. Either divide by spt*heads first, as dsk_xfer does, and take the remainder mod spt, or bank [dsk_base] mod spt once per transfer and add it to DX after the existing div.
findings.verify_note: Real, but the recommended 'add the base's low word into the dividend' is wrong twice: the low word alone does not preserve the phase mod spt, and a full 32-bit dividend can overflow the div. Recommendation and byte estimate corrected.

findings.title: dsk_find returns a redirected volume's name unterminated when the driver's is 13+ bytes
findings.detail: osapi_fs_ent forces a NUL at +15 for every listed entry, but dsk_find's FSV_ENUM arm joins .stage, which copies 13 bytes of the driver's staged name with no NUL forced; +13 is the attribute byte.
findings.recommendation: mov byte [es:di-1],0 after the rep movsb.
findings.verify_note: Confirmed at 8193-8199; the store with an ES override is 5 bytes, not 4.

findings.title: .bounce's 'no recursion' safety argument contradicts the fill and .img re-entries
findings.detail: The comment refuses a recursive dsk_xfer because fpg_busy 'can wait on a gfx lock'. But fpg_arm refuses rather than waits, and the fill and .img both re-enter dsk_xfer inside sch_lock. What can happen is the first chrome draw landing inside the lock with ES pinned, which the head of dsk_xfer says it avoids: a 1-sector miss below FPG_WARM followed by an inner 9-sector fill that crosses the threshold.
findings.recommendation: State the real reason (the head's no-draw-inside-the-lock rule, which fpg_arm's refusal does not change), and pass CX=0 to the inner fpg_busy for a fill so the rule holds there too.
findings.verify_note: The inconsistency is real. The reviewer's proposed reason ('[dsk_bnc_*] is one set of cells') is not one: the inner transfer would be into 512-aligned dsk_secbuf and could never bounce. The doc fix states the head's rule instead.

findings.title: A listing mount flushes every volume's cached chunks
findings.detail: dsk_rah_flush clears all records, so a Refresh or navigation on A: drops B:'s cache although B: has not changed. The .resig loop then stamps every record with the new disk's signature, which is safe only because the cache is empty. B:'s chunks would be safe to keep: each is keyed by its own disk's signature, re-checked at B:'s next mount.
findings.recommendation: Drop by volume with dsk_rah_wr(AX=0, CX=0FFFFh) (check its range arithmetic at that CX), and make .resig stamp only records whose RAH_VOL is [disk_drive].
findings.verify_note: dsk_rah_flush (7259) zeroes every RAH_N; .resig (4227-4233) stamps all DSK_RAH_RUNS records.

findings.title: The single-sector fallback also runs after a TIMEOUT (80h)
findings.detail: A drive-level timeout on a multi-sector run costs 3 attempts plus 3 more at one sector, each with a reset, and on a 5150 each costs seconds. The fallback exists for a bad sector; one sector will not fare better on a timeout. Most no-disk cases hit the mount's 1-sector LBA 0 read, which already stops at 3.
findings.recommendation: For 80h, one attempt at the run and then one at a single sector.
findings.verify_note: The failure arm tests only 03h before the ladder (2025-2027).

findings.title: dsk_boot_from's 255-head guard is dead
findings.detail: xor ah,ah / inc ax gives AX in 1..256 and never 0, so 'jz .nogeom ; DH = 0FFh is not a geometry' is never taken and 256 heads is accepted (legal CHS anyway).
findings.recommendation: Delete the guard, or use inc al if 256 heads is to be refused. Superseded by dr-1 if the AH=08h arm goes.
findings.verify_note: AL=DH, AH=0, inc ax: ZF only on 0FFFFh+1, unreachable. dsk_boot_from_x is in .ovl.

findings.title: dsk_fdd_probe clears unit 1's calibrated bit whatever unit it probed
findings.detail: .out ANDs 0040:003E with 7Dh ('re-seek unit 1'), but SPEC.md 18.98 made the probe run for units 1..3 (desk.inc:349 probes the externals and ignores their verdict). The probe RECALIBRATEs the unit it asked about, so the bit that should be cleared - forcing the BIOS to recalibrate before trusting its own idea of where the head is - is that unit's, not unit 1's.
findings.recommendation: Derive the mask from [fdd_unit]: clear bit [fdd_unit] and bit 7. Do not clear bit 7 only - the probe moves the head, so keeping a re-seek of the probed unit is the conservative half.
findings.verify_note: The wrong-unit mask is real (dsk_fdd_probe is .ovl). The reviewer's 'clear bit 7 only' option is refused: after a recalibrate the BIOS's own cylinder record can be stale, so the probed unit's bit should still be cleared. The comment at 10962 accurately describes the code, so its doc fix is refuted; it changes with the code.

findings.title: dsk_rah_fill reads [dsk_totsec] before the mount that sets it
findings.detail: The listing mount reads LBA 0 through a fill, which clamps against the previous volume's [dsk_totsec], or .bss garbage before the first FAT mount. Benign: the clamp can only shorten the fill (garbage 0 gives a one-sector request with no surplus, so no fill). But it is an unstated .bss read before write.
findings.recommendation: Comment it, or seed dsk_totsec = 0FFFFh in .text (a word moved from .bss).
findings.verify_note: dsk_totsec is resw in .bss (11325) and .vol reads it (7115).

findings.title: Documentation drift in this area is a defect of its own
findings.detail: About ten orphan contract headers for deleted routines (dsk_vol_kind, osapi_vol_paint, dsk_relist, dsk_copy_low, dsk_copy_out, dsk_put_icon, and dsk_sortdir's selection-sort header). Stale running counts (32 entries, 0..31, 64 on kern_big, the 128KB gate, unit 1). Retired designs described as current (FAT snapshot, one sector per call, disk_icons, disk_dir, dsk_relist, byte-identical boot sectors). SPEC 18 intro, its symbol tables and 18.3 describe the pre-18.91, pre-25.9 mount. checkdocs cannot see any of it.
findings.recommendation: Do one sweep (the doc_fixes here): fold the orphans into one-line 'lived here' notes, and name constants (DSK_NENT) instead of numbers.
findings.verify_note: Every quoted text was found exactly; 61 fixes confirmed (including seven the reviewer missed: disk_mount's LBA 0 geometry, SPEC's disk_mount row and cyl<80 gate, 18.3 step 3, dsk_chdir_q's dsk_relist, dskwin's 'disk_dir STAYS' and its 7,936-byte region), 2 refuted.

findings.title: dsk_up_open writes listing index 0 without consulting [dsk_nmax]
findings.detail: The '..' link is stored through dsk_put_dir (which has no bound) before the cap check. That is correct only because every aim supplies at least one entry (FS_VKB*32), and a store-less mount goes quiet before the listing, which is held by prose in another file.
findings.recommendation: Leave as is, or skip the link when [dsk_nmax] is 0.
findings.verify_note: dsk_put_dir does not check [dsk_nmax]; the zero-capacity case is excluded by the quiet stop at .listing.

findings.title: Mount and listing are one routine with quiet flags
findings.detail: disk_mount_x validates the volume, builds the caller's listing and harvests icons, and uses dsk_quiet and a zero dsk_dseg to switch the last two off. DOS, OS/2 and the Mac separate volume validation from directory listing. The code is already split at .listing.
findings.recommendation: Make disk_mount steps 1-2b and the scan/sort/harvest a separate routine that fmv_load calls; do it with dr-16's sweep. Needs files.inc's reviewer to agree the seam.
findings.prior_art: DOS media check / BDS against FindFirst/FindNext; Mac VCB against PBGetCatInfo loops owned by the Finder
findings.verify_note: The .quiet/.listing split at 4334-4347 exists as described; the redesign was not evaluated.

findings.title: Three caches where DOS has one buffer pool
findings.detail: The FAT window machinery (per-volume claims, pin, signatures, park/pick/want/evict/demote, dirty range; about 500 bytes .cold) sits beside a sector cache that already serves the window's loads. A unified buffer cache with dirty bits would delete it, but would lose the guaranteed DX/DX+1 residency that FAT12 straddles and dsk_next_clus's direct ES:BX reads rely on.
findings.recommendation: Record only: a large write-path rework for maybe -300 bytes.
findings.prior_art: DOS BUFFERS= holds FAT, directory and data sectors uniformly with a dirty bit and drive tag
findings.verify_note: Not checked; the ~500-byte and -300 figures are unverified estimates.

findings.title: Ask for the volume by name instead of silently dropping owed state
findings.detail: On a signature mismatch with state owed (a held WRITE_SEQ, a dirty FAT), the state is dropped silently (dws_hload, a window reload). With derived BS_VolID and a unique label, the kernel could toast 'Put back <label>' and refuse the write.
findings.recommendation: Record; about +40 bytes plus a toast string if taken.
findings.prior_art: Mac System 5-7 offline VCBs and 'Please insert the disk: <name>'; C64 GEOS disk name/ID check at OpenDisk
findings.verify_note: Not checked.

; are VOLUME-RELATIVE and 16-bit, exactly like a floppy's, and the driver adds

doc_fixes.new_text:

; machines ran; kern_big's carry a high word (OS88_BIGVOL, SPEC.md 18.7.5).
doc_fixes.why: OS88_BIGVOL gives kern_big 32-bit LBAs (disk.inc:100-105) and TotSec32 (5067-5076); rule 8 is rule 14's now (5124); dsk_xfer adds [dsk_vbase] (1490-1495, 1759-1760)

doc_fixes.new_text: a run failed 3 attempts and then its first sector 3 more, or
doc_fixes.why: after 3 strikes dsk_xfer retries one sector 3 times before .fail (disk.inc:2055-2066)

doc_fixes.old_text:
; LBA -> CHS with 16-bit div (LBA < 2880 so it never overflows):
;   cyl = LBA / (spt*heads); rem = LBA % (spt*heads)
;   head = rem / spt; sector = rem % spt + 1
; int 13h regs: CH = cyl low 8 (cyl < 80, no high bits), CL = sector,
; DH = head, DL = drive.
doc_fixes.new_text:
; LBA (plus the row's dsk_vbase, 0 except on a BIOS boot partition) -> CHS
; with one 32/16 div, refused when the quotient would pass a word or
; [dsk_cylmax] (80 on a floppy, 1024 on a fixed disk):
;   cyl = LBA / (spt*heads); rem = LBA % (spt*heads)
;   head = rem / spt; sector = rem % spt + 1
; int 13h regs: CH = cyl low 8, CL = sector | cyl bits 9:8 in bits 7:6 (0 on
; a floppy), DH = head, DL = the row's unit ([dsk_unit]).
doc_fixes.why: dsk_xfer adds [dsk_base], tests DX against spt*heads before one div and bounds by [dsk_cylmax] (disk.inc:1750-1767, 1555-1560) and packs cyl bits 9:8 into CL (1954-1961)

call** (AL=1) — no multi-sector calls, so track boundaries and DMA
alignment never matter. Each sector: up to 3 attempts, with AH=00 reset on
failure between attempts.
doc_fixes.new_text:
The LBA is volume-relative, plus the row's `dsk_vbase` on a BIOS boot
partition (§52.10.3). Transfers go in as few int 13h calls as the track (on
`kern_big`'s fixed disks the cylinder, §18.91.5), the 64KB DMA page and the
buffer allow (§18.91). Each run: up to 3 attempts, with an AH=00 reset
between them; a run that fails all three drops to one sector, which gets
three of its own.
doc_fixes.why: dsk_xfer batches runs (disk.inc:1784-1870) and falls back to dsk_run=1 after 3 failures (2055-2066); the table row three lines down already says so

doc_fixes.old_text:
2. **FAT snapshot.** Read `dsk_fatsz` sectors from `dsk_fatlba` into
   `FAT_SEG`:0 (ES=`FAT_SEG`, one `disk_read` call). On failure and
   `dsk_nfats`==2, retry once from FAT2 (`dsk_fatlba` + `dsk_fatsz`);
   both fail → mount fails. (FAT2 is the one redundancy FAT gives for
   free.)
doc_fixes.new_text:
2. **The FAT window** (§18.8). This volume's own window is reused on a
   quiet switch back to it whose boot-sector signature matches (§18.8.1,
   §18.8.2); otherwise the window is loaded at FAT sector 0 into
   `[dsk_fatseg]`, and on failure with `dsk_nfats`==2 retried once from
   FAT2; both fail → mount fails. (FAT2 is the one redundancy FAT gives for
   free.) Later windows fault in, with the same fallback.
   2a. A kept current directory (`dsk_chdir`) whose cluster is no longer
   allocated falls back to the root (§19.2).
   2b. A QUIET mount, or one with no destination (§22.6.3), stops here:
   `disk_nfiles` = 0 and the listing is marked stale.
doc_fixes.why: disk_mount_x: dsk_fatw_want/pick then dsk_fat_window (4276-4288); .cwd_lost zeroes [dsk_cwd] (4300-4310); .quiet when [dsk_quiet] or [dsk_dseg]=0 (4334-4346)

doc_fixes.old_text:
4. **Icon harvest.** For each accepted entry i: type≠1 → zero the 64-byte
   slot `disk_icons` + i×64 (ES=`LOW_SEG` `rep stosw`) — the generic-icon
   sentinel. Type=1 (cluster already validated, §19): `dsk_clus2lba`,
   `disk_read` 1 sector into `dsk_secbuf`; stage the 32 header bytes into
   `dsk_ent` via `dsk_copy_in`; if magic word @0 == 0x384F, version byte
   == 2 and flags bit 0 set, `dsk_copy_low` bytes 32..95 of `dsk_secbuf`
   → `disk_icons` + i×64; in every other case (read failure included)
   zero the slot. **Harvest failures are non-fatal** — the entry stays
   listed; a later load attempt reports the real error. `disk_icons` is
   fully rewritten every mount (preserves §29.1's rule that I_ICON may
   never point at it).
doc_fixes.new_text:
4. **Icon references** (§25.9). The listing's reference index is blanked
   to `ICO_R_NONE` (0xFF); then, per entry, `ico_ref_try` answers a folder
   or a body the machine-wide store already holds at no I/O, and only a
   miss on a type-1 package peeks its header (`dsk_peek`, through §18.95's
   cache): magic 0x384F, version == `PKG_FMT` and flags bit 0 set store
   bytes 32..95 as a body (`ico_put`). On `kern_big` at most
   `DSK_HARV_MAX` peeks per listing (§22.6.4), after the volume's
   `ASSOC.DAT` (§54.7) has been consulted. **Harvest failures are
   non-fatal** — the entry stays listed with the generic icon; a later load
   attempt reports the real error. `kern_dos` has no Disk window and no
   step 4 (§96.44.7).
doc_fixes.why: disk_mount_x blanks with 0xFF (4657-4668), calls asc_use_x, ico_ref_try, a DSK_HARV_MAX budget, dsk_peek_x and tests PKG_FMT (4700-4746); DSK_WANT_ICONS is off on KD_BUILD (dskwin.inc:283)
